correctness.rationale: The two displayed cubics are independently reconstructed from their integer coefficients. Exact Jacobian ideals prove each projective generator smooth once combined with squarefree leading binary forms. The base resultant has degree 9, is squarefree, and has exactly 9 real roots; shape position and the Jacobian determinant certify 9 transverse real base points. The gamma resultant has degree 21, is squarefree, and has exactly 21 real roots. Exact division by the base resultant gives a squarefree degree-12 quotient with exactly 12 real roots and no overlap with the base locus. Shape position makes these root counts point counts. Reduction of the nodal Hessian determinant is coprime to the quotient eliminant, so every extra critical point is an ordinary node. Exact elimination of the pencil parameter yields 12 distinct real critical values, and a separate homogeneous calculation rules out singularities at infinity. These checks establish the source genericity conditions and #S=12.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper explicitly asks whether its singular-start bound is sharp for all degree pairs and supplies witnesses only for (2,1), (2,2), (3,1), and (3,2). The equal cubic pair is the first natural omitted equal-degree case, and an exact integral witness is useful as a reproducible benchmark for the new cell-boundary framework. The certificate is stronger than a numerical picture: it proves all 9 base points and all 12 non-base critical points real and simple, verifies nodes and distinct critical values, and rules out infinity pathologies. Although classical real pencil theory already predicts existence, the coefficient-level benchmark directly inhabits the source's affine Newton-homotopy normalization and is therefore a motivated exact fact rather than an arbitrary slice.
